claims.text: The FeCoNiCrAl feedstock powder has a particle size of 5–30 μm.
The feedstock contains Al-rich and Cr-rich microsegregated regions.
The initial FeCoNiCrAl feedstock has a BCC random-solid-solution structure.
The grit-blasted Inconel 718 substrate has a surface roughness of Ra 3.9 ± 0.6 μm.
A medium air/fuel-pressure HVAF-i7 setting is optimal for depositing the FeCoNiCrAl bond coat.
The specified HVAF-i7 process will produce an approximately 150 μm thick FeCoNiCrAl coating.
The medium-pressure process will produce a highly dense coating with approximately 0.2% porosity.
The deposited coating will have a uniform elemental distribution.
The deposited coating will retain the BCC random-solid-solution structure.
The coating-substrate interface will contain an interdiffusion zone approximately 3 μm thick.
During oxidation, the coating will form a thin, dense, continuous Al2O3-based TGO.
The low-temperature HVAF-i7 process minimizes oxidation during deposition.
Low coating porosity restricts oxygen ingress and internal oxidation.
Outward diffusion of Al and its reaction with environmental oxygen forms a protective alumina scale.
Inherently slow diffusion in the FeCoNiCrAl HEA limits further oxide growth.
The absence of reactive elements such as Y or Hf may compromise oxide-scale adhesion under more severe exposure conditions.
Low- and high-pressure HVAF-i7 baseline coatings have porosities of 0.8% and 1.8%, respectively.
Literature HVAF-M3/MCrAlY coatings often have porosity above 6%.
Relative to the stated baselines, the medium-pressure coating will have a thinner TGO, slower oxidation kinetics, and less internal oxidation during 50-hour exposures at 1000–1150 °C.
Longer or hotter exposures may cause TGO spallation and reduced performance because the coating lacks reactive elements.

contradictions.description: The tests are called isothermal, but the conditions also specify approximately five-minute air-cooling cycles; repeated cooling would make the exposure cyclic or interrupted rather than strictly isothermal.
